card werk-cli-propose  [decided]
`werk propose`, `werk accept` and `werk discard` stage, commit and drop a change
why: A staged change needs one command to stage it, one to commit it and one to drop it. The ✓ in the map runs the same accept.

```
werk propose <id> [--title "..."] [--why "..."] [--ops '[{"tag": ...}]']
werk accept <id> --actor you
werk discard <id>
```

- `--ops` is a JSON list. A tag is `elaborated` {old, new}, `new` {new}, or `removed` {old}.
- Every block of the current body must be the `old` of an op. Keep a block unchanged with an `elaborated` op whose old and new are equal. Otherwise the command fails and prints the blocks at risk (#al-diff-cli-cover).
- An `old` that does not quote a real block is shown as removed plus new, never trusted (#al-diff-cli).
- `werk accept` fails without `--actor you`. The ✓ in the map appends the same event (#al-diff-cli-btn). Accepting a ghost also accepts its ghost refines parents, options and sources (#werk-propose-new).
- `werk discard` on a ghost also drops its ghost children.

  -> refines         werk-cli  The CLI is the agent's interface to the map. Each command's form lives on one card under it

  -> depends_on      al-diff-cli-cover  An op list that leaves a block unnamed is refused, not applied

  -> depends_on      werk-propose-new  A new card is a proposal too, not a direct append

This is a decision bug. The code does what the card says.

- #al-diff-render says: "A block that changes shape shows the old block removed and the new block added."
- The diff code reads "shape" as the line count of the list. One added bullet changes the count. So the whole list counts as a new shape, and the diff strikes the full list and adds it again below.
- The code pairs list items one by one only when the old list and the new list have the same number of lines.

I staged an edit on #al-diff-render with a new rule: the diff pairs the old and new items one by one, so it marks only the added, removed or reworded item. Only a block that changes kind, such as a paragraph that becomes a list, is replaced whole. The old reading is now the rejected option #al-diff-render:opt0.

A list diff now marks only the item that changed. An added item gets a highlight. A removed item gets a highlight and a strikethrough. The other items stay plain.

To see it, reload the map and open a card that has a pending edit to a list, for example #werk.

- **Reworded item:** an old item pairs with a new item when the two items share at least half their words. The diff then marks only the changed words, in place.
- **Unrelated item:** if an item shares less than half its words, the diff shows it as one removed item and one added item.
- **Numbered list:** if an item is removed, the items after it are renumbered. A renumbered item still counts as unchanged.
- **Paragraph to list:** a block that changes kind, such as a paragraph that becomes a list, is still replaced whole. This is what #al-diff-render now says.
